content.user_title: Build Persistent Azure AI Agents with .NET
content.value_statement: Persistent agent workflows require coordinated threads, messages, runs, tools, and cleanup. This skill provides focused .NET patterns for implementing those workflows with Azure AI Agents.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation and environment configuration for Azure AI Agents Persistent.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential authentication and PersistentAgentsClient creation.
Explains agent, thread, message, polling, and streaming workflows in C#.
Provides examples for function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search.
Lists key SDK types, tool definitions, and streaming update reasons.
Demonstrates resource cleanup and Azure request error handling.
limitations: Uses prerelease package guidance that may change as Azure SDK versions evolve.
Assumes an existing Azure AI project, deployed model, and valid service connections.
Provides illustrative snippets, not a complete application or deployment configuration.
Does not implement authorization, input validation, observability, retries, or production security controls.

use_cases.title: Create a Persistent Agent
use_cases.description: Build a C# workflow that creates an agent, thread, message, and run, then retrieves the response.

use_cases.title: Design Tool-Enabled Agents
use_cases.description: Compare function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search before selecting an integration approach.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Agent Runs
use_cases.description: Review polling, streaming updates, run statuses, cleanup, and request errors while diagnosing an Azure agent integration.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up the SDK
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to configure a .NET project for Azure AI Agents Persistent using environment variables and DefaultAzureCredential.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new C# project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C# example that creates an agent, thread, user message, run, and prints the final response.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a first end-to-end persistent agent.

prompt_templates.title: Add Retrieval and Streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a C# workflow combining file search with streaming responses and cleanup for files, vector stores, threads, and agents.
prompt_templates.scenario: Extend an agent with document retrieval and live output.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Tool Calling Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my agent design and add function validation, authorization, timeouts, status handling, retries, logging, and deterministic cleanup.
prompt_templates.scenario: Harden an advanced tool-enabled workflow for production review.

output_examples.input: Create a persistent math tutor workflow.
output: Agent, thread, message, and run sequence

output_examples.input: Compare polling and streaming for agent runs.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison covering response latency, implementation complexity, status handling, failure behavior, and suitable user experiences.

output_examples.input: Add document search to an existing agent.
output: File upload and vector store workflow

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and keep endpoints, deployment names, and connection identifiers outside source code.
Handle every terminal and actionable run status, including failures, cancellation, expiration, and required tool outputs.
Delete temporary threads, agents, files, and vector stores, preferably with deterministic cleanup after failures.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch model-requested functions without strict name allowlists, argument validation, authorization, and execution limits.
Do not poll continuously without delays, timeouts, cancellation support, and bounded retries.
Do not upload sensitive files or enable external search tools without access controls and data governance review.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It guides persistent Azure AI agent workflows in C#, including threads, messages, runs, streaming, tools, retrieval, cleanup, and errors.

faq.question: What Azure resources do I need?
faq.answer: You need an Azure AI project endpoint, a deployed model, credentials, and any service connections required by selected tools.

faq.question: Which package version does the guide use?
faq.answer: The guide mentions stable 1.1.0 and preview 1.2.0-beta.8. Verify current NuGet versions before installation.

faq.question: Does it cover polling and streaming?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates status polling, message retrieval, streaming updates, and basic completion handling.

faq.question: Which agent tools are included?
faq.answer: Examples cover code interpreter, function calling, file search, Bing grounding, and Azure AI Search, with additional tools listed for reference.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Add validation, authorization, retries, observability, testing, and current SDK verification before production use.
